headline: Shalimar Paints Limited announces Qualified Institutional Placement
sum: Shalimar Paints has notified stock exchanges of a Qualified Institutional Placement. Details on issue size, price and allottee composition remain subject to board approval and regulatory clearance.
implication: QIP under Chapter VIII of SEBI ICDR Regulations permits accelerated capital raising from qualified investors without shareholder approval; counsel must verify pricing mechanism (floor or fixed), post-allotment lock-in (1 year minimum), and continuous disclosure obligations during offer period.
detail: Shalimar Paints notified both NSE and BSE of its intent to undertake a QIP on 13 August 2026. As a listed paint company, the QIP will be subject to SEBI's Institutional Placement Framework and requires board approval of the issue size, offer price band and timeline. The offer will be open only to Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) including mutual funds, FIIs, insurance companies and eligible banks, ensuring a broad institutional cap table.

framework.ref: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, Chapter VIII
framework.note: Central—governs QIP process, pricing mechanism (floor price rule), allottee eligibility (QIBs only), and disclosures.

framework.ref: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, Regulation 106–108
framework.note: Central—sets timeline, shareholder approval waiver, pricing rules and quantum limits for QIP.
Central—authorization for issuance of securities by board; QIP shares issued under board authority.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Section 42 (private placement exemption applicability)
framework.note: QIP does not require private placement license but must comply with institutional buyer definition.

framework.ref: Listing Regulations (SEBI Listing Rules, 2015), Chapter V (Capital Structure)
framework.note: Governs listing continuity, stock exchange disclosures, and post-allotment regulatory filings.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 112 (capital gains on listed shares)
framework.note: QIP shares held by institutional investors subject to long-term capital gains regime.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 (if FII participation)
framework.note: FII investors must comply with FPI registration and investment limits if subscribing.

conditions: Board approval of issue size, price band and timeline
SEBI pricing approval (if floor price rule applicable)
Allotment and credit to demat accounts
One-year post-allotment lock-in (mandatory for promoter/promoter group entities if any)
approvals: Board of Directors (issue size, price, timeline)
SEBI (pricing mechanism review if floor price triggered)
structure.novel: QIP mechanism allows price discovery among institutional investors without shareholder vote; accelerates capital raising for listed companies with strong institutional backing.

triggers.law: SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, Chapter VIII
triggers.note: Mandatory regulatory trigger for institutional placement; pricing floor and QIB eligibility verified pre-allotment.
Continuous disclosure and insider trading compliance during offer window.
